title: Flow Perturbation++: Multi-Step Unbiased Jacobian Estimation for High-Dimensional Boltzmann Sampling
claim: Estimating a transformation's determinant in one shot is high-variance; decomposing it into sequential steps with per-step estimates and multiplying them fixes this.
layout: 2 panels split by dashed line; top-to-bottom flow, formulas below each panel
description: A two-panel block diagram separated by a vertical dashed line. Panel (a), on the left, is the single-step baseline. A beige latent box z feeds down into a green box labeled Flow f(z), which outputs a gray x box below. A side arrow labeled x leads from the flow box to a yellow Estimation box, which produces the estimate J_FP. The one-shot formula, a norm of the inverse Jacobian times epsilon raised to the power -D, sits underneath. Panel (b), on the right, is the multi-step version. A latent z(x_{T+1}) feeds a vertical stack of green flow blocks (T, ..., 1). Each block passes its intermediate x_k to its own yellow Estimation block, which outputs J_FP,k. The stack ends at a gray x(x_1) box. Below it, the J_FP++ formula is written as a product over k=1..T of the per-step estimates. Green, yellow and beige color-code the module types. The eye goes first to the repeated stack in (b).
caption: Flow Perturbation vs FP++. (a) Single-step FP estimates the full-flow determinant in one shot, which can lead to high variance. (b) FP++ decomposes flow into T steps and applies determinant estimation sequentially from latent z = xT +1 to x = x1. The product of per-step estimates yields the FP++ determinant estimator.
abstract: The scalability of continuous normalizing flows (CNFs) for unbiased Boltzmann sampling remains limited in high-dimensional systems due to the cost of Jacobian-determinant evaluation, which requires $D$ backpropagation passes through the flow layers. Existing stochastic Jacobian estimators such as the Hutchinson trace estimator reduce computation but introduce bias, while the recently proposed Flow Perturbation method is unbiased yet suffers from high variance. We present \textbf{Flow Perturbation++}, a variance-reduced extension of Flow Perturbation that discretizes the probability-flow ODE and performs unbiased stepwise Jacobian estimation at each integration step. This multi-step construction retains the unbiasedness of Flow Perturbation while achieves substantially lower estimator variance. Integrated into a Sequential Monte Carlo framework, Flow Perturbation++ achieves significantly improved equilibrium sampling on a 1000D Gaussian Mixture Model and the all-atom Chignolin protein compared with Hutchinson-based and single-step Flow Perturbation baselines.
